body:
Today's scan found no cross-platform arbitrage: zero opportunities across Kalshi and Polymarket gold contracts. Order books line up sensibly with each other, so there's nothing to flag on the mechanics side — just a quiet day for the tracker.

The more notable thing is simply where gold sits. Kalshi's September 2026 settlement ladder crosses 50% around the $4,390–$4,410 strikes (the $4,370.99 strike bids 0.51/asks 0.54, while $4,410.99 bids 0.46/asks 0.50), implying traders see spot near that level already. That lines up with actual spot: as of Sep 09, 2026 at 1:00 AM EDT, the live Gold spot price for 1 ounce of Gold in U.S. dollars was $4,395.16, according to JM Bullion. Polymarket's touch contracts tell the same story — the September low-touch market for $4,300 is priced near even money (0.65/0.66) since spot has already been well above that level, while touches of $4,000 (0.13/0.16) and $3,900 (0.04/0.07) get progressively cheaper, a sensible monotonic curve rather than a mispricing.

The scale of the move is real, not a data glitch: both gold and silver enjoyed record-smashing rallies in 2025, surging 66% and 135% respectively over the course of the year, according to CNBC, and the climb has continued into 2026 on record inflows into gold-backed exchange traded funds (ETFs), along with strong demand for bars and coins and central-bank buying, according to Yahoo Finance UK. Some thin weekly Polymarket strikes (e.g., the week-of-Sept-7 $4,250 touch market, bid 0.04/ask 0.33) show wide spreads purely from low volume, not genuine free money — a reminder that a wide quote on a low-liquidity book is a market-depth issue, not an edge.
headline: No cross-platform gold arbitrage found; Kalshi and Polymarket pricing align near $4,395 spot
